title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) comparing a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline to accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and a deterministic validator we selected K=200 tasks by a reproducible SHA‑256 sorting rule and evaluated a single shared generator output per task in both arms. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair step was never invoked. We release full execution and scoring artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...) and verifier traces so others can replay and extend the evaluation. We interpret this outcome as a ceiling/null case for the tested model/validator/task sampling regime and discuss implications for future failure‑rich evaluations.

sections.introduction:
Automating the translation from high‑level operator intent to device configuration promises operational speedups but risks introducing regressions (reachability loss, service interruption). A widely proposed architectural remedy is the generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline: an LLM proposes configuration commands, a deterministic verifier checks safety and semantic constraints, and a repair step attempts to correct any violations before apply. While prior work advocates such pipelines and demonstrates tooling prototypes, causal estimates of the verifier’s marginal effect under reproducible, preregistered conditions remain sparse.

We preregistered (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256: a6d73a5c...) and executed a paired experiment that isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect. Our confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the per‑task difference in the binary validator pass rate when the same generated candidate is (i) accepted directly (baseline) vs (ii) passed through verify→repair first (guarded). To isolate generator variability we used a single shared initial generation per task (shared_initial_generation) that both conditions evaluated; guarded could invoke one repair call only if the candidate failed validation (maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1). The requested model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: 1acce9255...). All execution, provider traces, and scoring JSONs are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...).

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired confirmatory run and analysis. (2) An artifact‑grounded report of a ceiling/null outcome (no discordant pairs observed). (3) Operational guidance for designing future verifier utility evaluations that avoid ceiling regimes.
sections.related_work: LLM assistance for configuration generation and agentic NetOps is an active area (surveys and recent benchmarks emphasize generate–validate–repair architectures and formal verification; see Cornetto and related generate–validate–repair position papers). Prior systems integrate symbolic verifiers (e.g., Batfish/Veriflow variants) or model translation to solvers; other work argues for confining LLMs to translation and relying on solvers for reasoning. Our work differs by providing a preregistered paired causal estimate of the verifier’s marginal effect under a deterministic sampling and execution contract, with full provenance and replay artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 a6d73a5c...) before observing final outcomes. The primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes, supplemented by a paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for a 95% percentile CI.

Task generation and deterministic sampling. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and filtered to those covered by the preregistered deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). To avoid human selection bias the manifest applied a deterministic selection rule: compute SHA‑256(intent_string), sort ascending, and take the first K=200 unique tasks (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256: f1d447b7...). This procedure and the manifest are archived and reproducible.

Shared initial generation and arm semantics. For each task a single generator call (shared_initial_generation) produced candidate_c which was used unchanged in both conditions. Baseline: candidate_c is accepted as the apply proposal and scored by the deterministic validator post‑apply. Guarded: candidate_c is first run through the deterministic validator; if violations are detected, the pipeline permits at most one repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1) to produce a repaired candidate which the validator then rechecks; if the repaired candidate still fails or no repair is permitted, the episode is scored accordingly. The shared initial design isolates the verifier’s marginal effect on a fixed generator output but prevents adaptive regeneration by the generator in response to validator feedback; this design choice was preregistered and is discussed below as a key constraint on interpretation.

Models, tooling, and artifact capture. Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The deterministic validator parses generated text into structured field changes, enforces workflow constraints (protected interfaces, must_be_down_for_fields, group minima), and returns a binary valid flag along with detailed diagnostics (observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, final_state snapshot). Every provider call, model prompt/response, scoring JSON, and computed hash was archived. Key artifact fingerprints: raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4..., execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256 = 79c91155..., model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce925..., and master prompt reference at provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e....

Statistical plan for the degenerate outcome. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nontrivial baseline failure rate (~0.20). In paired designs, when there are zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0), the paired estimate is exactly zero and the exact McNemar two‑sided p equals 1.00; the paired bootstrap over empirical paired outcomes will produce a degenerate percentile CI [0.00,0.00] if every bootstrap replicate reproduces identical counts. We executed the planned bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) and report the exact degenerate CI accordingly (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 52a0858d...). This is the appropriate descriptive inference given the observed ceiling.
sections.results:
Execution and provenance. Planned episodes: 400 (two arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400. Model calls used: 200 (single shared initial generator per task; repair calls were never invoked). No provider or infrastructure failures affected the scientific run. Raw results and per‑task scoring JSONs are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...). Representative scoring JSONs are listed in execution/scoring/ (e.g., task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). Complete paired counts: complete_pairs = 200. Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The guarded repair pathway was never needed: repair_applied=false for every guarded episode in execution/scoring/*.json.

Representative task diagnostics. Each scoring JSON contains validator diagnostics: parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot, and difficulty metadata. For example, execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json records parsed_command_count=4, observed_touched_field_count=3, normalized_configuration equal to the candidate, and validator.valid=true. Six representative tasks and their difficulty annotations are embedded in the archived representative_tasks manifest; within that small representative set the difficulty composition was medium=1, hard=2, very_hard=3. The full per‑task difficulty metadata for all K=200 tasks is present in execution/scoring/*.json and can be deterministically aggregated by replaying those JSONs; the run archive intentionally preserved per‑task metadata rather than producing a single aggregated histogram during execution (see analysis artifact list).

Why repairs were not invoked. Three artifact‑grounded factors explain the null/ceiling outcome: (1) the deterministic sampling rule required validator coverage for inclusion, which biases the sample toward intents the validator already supports; (2) the requested LLM (gpt-5-mini) produced candidates that respected the explicit task workflow constraints encoded in the task payloads (observed in per‑task normalized_configuration equals the reference); (3) the shared_initial_generation design fixes the generator output across both arms and therefore prevents generator adaptation to validator feedback; repairs can be invoked only when the initial candidate fails validation. All provider calls, candidates, and validator traces are archived and hashed to support audit (execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/responses/*.txt; execution/scoring/*.json).

Reproducibility artifacts. The full set of artifacts required to exactly replay the run are archived: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce925...), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = 79c91155...), and the preregistration (SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...). The master prompt used to initiate autonomous behavior is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). Deterministic reconciliation confirms no cross‑condition cache key reuse and consistent episode accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and scope. The observed ceiling/null outcome (no discordant pairs) is a valid empirical observation under the preregistered contract: the verifier could have reduced regressions only if failing initial candidates were present. Because baseline failure rate = 0.0, the preregistered power calculation (which assumed baseline ≈ 0.20) does not apply post hoc; exact paired inference and the bootstrap CI fully describe the observed uncertainty.

Design lessons for future evaluations (artifact‑grounded guidance). To detect verifier/repair utility in confirmatory paired estimates, future studies should (and our archived artifacts support each recommendation):
1) Sample failure‑rich distributions. Include historical misconfigurations or construct adversarial/boundary intents that are within validator coverage but challenge generators. The execution archive contains per‑task difficulty and validator coverage flags (execution/scoring/*.json) so investigators can quantify baseline failure prevalence before committing to a confirmatory sample.
2) Vary generator strengths. Evaluate multiple LLMs (including weaker models) so the baseline error rate becomes nonzero and repairs can be exercised. The run’s single requested_model (gpt-5-mini) and its configuration are archived (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...).
3) Consider interactive generator–verifier estimands. If the objective is closed‑loop end‑to‑end improvement with on‑the‑fly regeneration, the estimand changes and the shared_initial design is not appropriate; our archive preserves the shared_initial responses and shows how to replay that alternative design by allowing regeneration and logging further model calls.
4) Publish per‑task validator coverage and difficulty aggregates together with paired counts. Per‑task metadata exists in execution/scoring/*.json and was intentionally retained to enable post hoc aggregation by independent auditors.

Statistical interpretation of the degenerate CI. When every observed pair is concordant the bootstrap reproduces identical empirical pairs and the percentile CI becomes a point mass [0.00,0.00]; the McNemar exact test yields p=1.00. This does not imply the verifier is universally unnecessary — it implies that under the particular controlled sampling rule and model the initial candidates already satisfied the validator constraints. The evidence is therefore a ceiling/null result specific to the tested task/model/validator regime.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a fully artifact‑archived paired evaluation of a verifier+repair pipeline versus accepting LLM candidates directly. Under the deterministic sampling rule and requested_model (gpt-5-mini), all shared generator candidates passed the deterministic validator: baseline = 200/200; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair path was never invoked. This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the provided artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...); it does not generalize to failure‑rich production settings. We therefore recommend that future confirmatory evaluations intentionally sample or construct failure‑rich tasks, vary generator strengths, and consider interactive closed‑loop estimands if the goal is to measure end‑to‑end verifier utility. All execution artifacts, scoring traces, and the master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...) are released for replay and audit to support cumulative, rigorous evaluation in the NetOps domain.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Synthetic deterministic task pool and the preregistered inclusion rule (validator coverage required) limit external validity to production intent distributions that contain emergent or historical misconfigurations.
Construct validity is tied to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; if the validator lacks coverage for real regression modes, the binary outcome conflates true safety with validator reach.

Design constraint: shared_initial_generation fixes generator outputs across arms and prevents generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates, not closed‑loop generator–verifier improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable; inference is descriptive and artifact‑grounded for the tested regime.
